reason: The front of the arm has a biceps slot, and the introduction says to build it from muscle cells.
expectation: The muscle cells should build or begin building the biceps at the front of the arm.

alternatives.reason: The bone attachment also needs mineral, and the introduction says either order works.

effect: The muscle cells formed the biceps, but the radius still needs mineral.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the cells become muscle fibres; the bone part is still unfinished.
reason: The front attachment is still awaiting mineral, so I’ll strengthen it next.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone at the biceps attachment.

alternatives.reason: I could build the triceps before finishing the front.

effect: The front is complete: mineral strengthens the radius, and the biceps pulls it to bend the elbow.
reaction: The demonstration makes the connection between muscle pull and bone movement clearer.
reason: The back still needs a triceps, and the introduction says it can be built from the same kind of muscle cells.
expectation: The muscle cells should form the triceps at the back of the arm.

alternatives.reason: I could strengthen the back attachment first; either order works.

effect: The triceps is built, but the ulna at its attachment still needs mineral.
reaction: The back follows the same understandable pattern as the front.
reason: The remaining goal is to strengthen the triceps bone attachment.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the ulna and complete the triceps attachment.

effect: The back is complete: the triceps pulls on the strengthened ulna to straighten the elbow. Both goals are finished.
reaction: The matching demonstration made it clear how the same kind of muscle cells can produce a different movement.

mostWorthwhile.text: Completing the back was most worthwhile because comparing it with the front showed how tendon attachment changes the effect of a muscle's pull.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps repeated the familiar muscle-cell step, though it set up the useful comparison.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that the same kind of muscle cells could help bend or straighten the elbow depending on where the muscle attaches.

arbitrary.text: None felt especially arbitrary: the slots and pictures made the muscle and mineral pairings clear.

continue.text: I would try another chapter to see more connections between body structures and their jobs, though I hope it offers less repetition.
